mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a downturn in economic activity and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the quarters following a GDPC1 decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) signals supply-side constraints, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when INDPRO drops > 1%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth expectations improve.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when PAYEMS and UNRATE meet the trigger conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals an increase in demand for housing, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economy benefits from increased construction activity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when HOUST increases > 10%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) combined with a decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a disinflationary environment with accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns improve.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS decreases > 0.25% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS meet the trigger conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real final sales of domestic product (RSAFS) signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of the quarters following a RSAFS increase, the hypothesis is rejected.
